Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: A grandchild brings up a general question about navigating a new phase of their life.
Situation2: They travel a long distance to participate in an important religious festival, ensuring they fully engage in all rituals and offerings.
Story: I sat on the train, the rhythmic clatter echoing my restless thoughts. My suitcase was packed with gifts and offerings for the festival, and my mind was already rehearsing the prayers I would recite. This festival was important—my presence was expected, my participation in every ritual a matter of family pride and religious duty. Just as I was settling into the journey, my phone buzzed. It was my granddaughter, her voice trembling with uncertainty. She was facing a big decision about her future, and she needed my guidance. She asked if I could come over, just to talk, to share the wisdom she trusted I had. I felt the weight of her need, the unspoken expectation that I would be there for her, as I always had been. But the festival was tomorrow, and missing it would disappoint my family and go against my devotion. My heart pulled in two directions—toward the sacred rituals of my faith, and toward the child who needed me. I stared out the window, torn, the train carrying me forward as my mind wrestled with which role I owed more.
